newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan sells 80,000 T U.S. corn to local traders.
newsitem.headline: Jordan sells 80,000 T U.S. corn to local traders.

text.p: Jordan has sold 80,000 tonnes of U.S. Number 3 yellow corn or better to local traders ahead of a move to end a state monopoly on imports of the commodity and allow private firms to handle it, traders said on Wednesday.
Jordan's Ministry of Supply sold corn to six local trading firms - 30,000 tonnes were already stored in its silos and another 50,000 tonnes are expected to be shipped this month.

It sold the 30,000 tonnes of corn it had stored since September at 139.5 dinars($197) a tonne FOT from its Amman or Irbid silos. The second quantity of 50,000 tonnes was sold at 116 dinars ($164) per tonne FOT Aqaba.

The government last year ended its monopoly on imports of rice, sugar, and yellow corn to allow private sector purchases. But it temporarily stopped private imports of yellow corn until it disposed of its contracted quantities.
Traders will still have to sell the yellow corn at a fixed retail selling price of 148 dinars ($209) a tonne.
Jordan has an annual consumption of yellow corn of around 500,000 tonnes.
